results.title: AWS vs Azure vs GCP Cloud GPU Pricing [2026]
results.author: Sana Rahman
highlights:
Cloud GPU pricing used to be a simple spreadsheet exercise: look up the hourly rate for an H100 instance, multiply by the hours you need, pick the cheapest provider. In October 2026 that spreadsheet broke. AWS raised its Blackwell B200 Capacity Block rate by roughly 15% on October 7, Microsoft Azure is one of the only major clouds still publishing a flat per-GPU hourly rate for H100 capacity, and Google Cloud has yet to post an official list price for H100, H200 or B200 instances at all. Comparing AWS vs Azure vs GCP cloud GPU pricing now means comparing three different billing philosophies, not just three price tags.

...

Microsoft Azure, by contrast, still publishes retail, pay-as-you-go rates for specific H100 virtual machine sizes. That transparency makes Azure the easiest provider to quote cleanly in a comparison article, which is exactly why most of the concrete numbers in this piece come from Azure’s own SKUs. Google Cloud sits at the opposite end: its A3 (H100), A3 Ultra (H200) and A4 (B200) instance families are confirmed to exist and to use those specific Nvidia GPUs, but no official Google Cloud page in the current research set states a public hourly price for any of them. Google increasingly routes customers toward Flex-start scheduling and committed-use contracts instead of a posted rate.

...

## Azure GPU Lineup: NC40ads, ND96isr H100 v5 and ND96isr H200 v5

Azure’s current GPU VM lineup for AI training includes NC40ads H100 v5, ND96isr H100 v5 and ND96isr H200 v5. Two of those SKUs give us the cleanest published numbers in this entire comparison. The NC40ads H100 v5 size, a single-H100 configuration, carried a reported East US pay-as-you-go Linux rate of $6.98 per hour as of October 19, 2026. The larger ND96isr H100 v5 size, which packs eight H100 GPUs, was reported at $98.32 per VM-hour in East US on the same date, which works out to $12.29 per GPU-hour.

Azure also lists an ND96isr H200 v5 size with eight H200 GPUs carrying 141 GB of memory each, making it the newest Hopper-class GPU family Azure has confirmed. Microsoft has not published an officially confirmed Azure B200 virtual machine family or hourly price as of October 23, 2026. Separately, Microsoft Foundry’s managed-compute tier, still in preview, bills hourly per accelerator across A100, H100, H200 and MI300 GPU families, but Microsoft’s documentation says rates vary by accelerator family, region, deployment scope and commitment term, and directs customers to the Azure Pricing Calculator rather than a published table.

...

## Cloud GPU Pricing Compared: What’s Published vs What’s a Black Box

This is the table that matters most for anyone trying to budget an AI training run, and it is deliberately conservative: it only includes rates that each provider has actually published, rather than third-party estimates.

| GPU | AWS (published rate) | Azure (published rate) | Google Cloud (published rate) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100, single GPU | No flat rate published; Capacity Blocks price dynamically | $6.98/hour, NC40ads H100 v5, East US, captured Oct. 19, 2026 | Not published |
| H100, 8-GPU node | No flat rate published | $98.32/hour ($12.29/GPU-hour), ND96isr H100 v5, East US, captured Oct. 19, 2026 | Not published |
| H200, 8-GPU node | No flat rate published | No flat on-demand VM rate confirmed in official sources | Not published |
| B200, per GPU-hour (Capacity Block) | $14.208/hour, effective Oct. 7, 2026, up from $12.355/hour (about a 15% increase) | Not offered / not confirmed | Not published; A4 uses Flex-start scheduling instead of a flat rate |

...

The single clearest pricing move any of the three providers made in the last three months was AWS’s. Effective October 7, 2026, AWS raised its P6-B200 Capacity Block price from $12.355 to $14.208 per accelerator-hour, an increase of approximately 15%, according to GPU-pricing trackers Axis Intelligence and Dev.to’s FastGPU column, which independently captured the same before-and-after figures. For an eight-GPU P6-B200 node, the current instance-hour rate is about $113.666, a noticeable jump in monthly spend for teams running sustained training jobs.

results.title: GPU rental prices in 2026: H100, H200 and B200 per hour
results.author: Safeguard Security Team
highlights:
In October 2026, published on-demand list prices for an H100 ranged from about $2 to about $12 per GPU-hour, depending on the provider, the billing model and what is bundled. Specialist clouds mostly sit between $3 and $6. Spot and long commitments can cut the price by half or more. B200 list prices run from about $6 to $14.

...

- AWS Capacity Blocks, p5.48xlarge (8 H100s), N. Virginia, Ohio and Oregon: $47.757 per instance-hour, $5.970 per GPU-hour. AWS Capacity Blocks pricing page, 19 October 2026.
- AWS p5.48xlarge on-demand (8 H100s), N. Virginia, Ohio, Oregon: $6.88 per GPU-hour, as checked by IntuitionLabs on 10 October 2026.
- Azure NC40ads H100 v5 (1 GPU), East US, Linux pay-as-you-go: $6.98 per hour. Azure ND96isr H100 v5 (8 GPUs): $98.32 per VM-hour, $12.29 per GPU-hour. Azure Retail Prices API, 19 October 2026.
- Google Cloud a3-highgpu-8g (8 H100s), Iowa, on-demand: $88.49 per VM-hour, which is $11.06 per GPU-hour. IntuitionLabs, 10 October 2026.
- Oracle Cloud BM.GPU.H100.8: $10.00 per GPU-hour list. IntuitionLabs, 10 October 2026.
- CoreWeave HGX H100, 8 GPUs, on-demand: $49.24 per instance-hour, about $6.16 per GPU. CoreWeave pricing page, 19 October 2026.
- Lambda H100 SXM, 8-GPU instance: $3.99 per GPU-hour. Lambda pricing page, 19 October 2026. IntuitionLabs records $2.99 in a 2025 snapshot.
- Runpod H100 SXM: $3.99 Secure Cloud and $2.69 Community Cloud. H100 PCIe: $1.99 Community Cloud. Runpod pricing page, 19 October 2026.
- Nebius HGX H100 on demand: $4.50 per GPU-hour. Nebius prices page, 19 October 2026. IntuitionLabs says this took effect on 1 October 2026, up from $3.85.
- H200 on-demand list prices: $5.29 (Runpod Secure Cloud), $5.40 (Nebius), about $6.31 (CoreWeave, $50.44 per 8-GPU instance). Provider pages, 19 October 2026.
- B200 on-demand list prices: $6.69 (Lambda, 8 GPUs), $7.99 (Runpod Secure Cloud), $8.50 (Nebius), $8.60 (CoreWeave, $68.80 per 8-GPU instance). AWS Capacity Blocks: $14.208. Provider pages, 19 October 2026.
- B200 index price: $2.31 per hour in early March 2026 and $4.95 in late April 2026, per the Ornn Compute Price Index as reported on tomtunguz.com on 27 April 2026.

...

The large clouds charge the most on-demand. IntuitionLabs lists AWS at $6.88 per GPU-hour for the 8-GPU instance in three US regions and $8.60 in N. California. Azure's own price feed shows $6.98 for a single-GPU VM and $98.32 for the 8-GPU VM in East US, which is $12.29 per GPU. IntuitionLabs lists Google at $11.06 per GPU in Iowa and Oracle at $10.00.

...

Several of these went up. According to the survey, AWS Capacity Blocks rose from $5.19 to $5.97, Runpod Secure Cloud H100 SXM from $3.29 to $3.99, Lambda's 8-GPU SXM from $2.99 (a 2025 snapshot) to $3.99, and Nebius's HGX H100 from $3.85 to $4.50 effective 1 October 2026. The current figures match the providers' own pages on 19 October 2026. The survey says AWS on-demand and Azure list prices were not re-verified as lower than the 2025 third-party figures.

results.title: GPU Prices 2026: H100 From $3.49/hr, RTX 5070 at +58%
results.author: Axis Intelligence Research
highlights:
> Prices verified on October 2, 2026. Every price on this page was read from the vendor’s live pricing page, public price API or retail listing on that date. AWS Capacity Block rates effective October 7, 2026 are taken from AWS’s own announcement on its pricing page.

Renting one NVIDIA H100 for an hour costs $3.49 on Runpod and $12.29 on Microsoft Azure — the same chip, listed on public pricing pages on October 2, 2026. Axis Intelligence Research’s GPU Hour Premium Ratio puts the hyperscaler list premium at 2.93x the neocloud median, and AWS is raising every GPU Capacity Block rate by roughly 15% on October 7.

4. The cheapest new GeForce RTX 5070 on Newegg cost $869.99 on October 2, 2026, 58% above the $549 price NVIDIA announced at CES in January 2025.

results.title: Neocloud vs hyperscaler GPU: what capacity costs | Casitel
highlights:
## What the rate cards say

All rates below are US dollars per GPU-hour, taken from each provider's own page on 3 November 2026. They are list rates. They are not what large buyers sign.

Provider H100 H200 B200 What the rate is

Lambda$3.99 Not listed$6.69 On-demand, 8-GPU instance

E2E Networks$3.99$5.29$7.99 On-demand

Nebius$4.50$5.40$8.50 On-demand, HGX

CoreWeave$6.16$6.31$8.60 On-demand, North America

AWS$5.97$6.87$14.21 Capacity Blocks, a short reservation

Google Cloud$9.80$10.71 Not read Vertex AI, managed service

Oracle$10.00$10.00$14.00 Pay as you go

Microsoft Azure$12.29 Not read Not read ND H100 v5, East US

Three of these need a note. CoreWeave and Azure price a whole 8-GPU machine by the hour: $49.24 and $98.32 for the H100. The per-GPU figures above are our own arithmetic. AWS publishes a plain on-demand rate only in its calculator, so the AWS row is its Capacity Blocks price, and for the H200 it is the p5e machine (the p5en costs $7.90). Google's row is the Vertex AI managed service, which is not the same product as a bare virtual machine.

Even so, the spread is wide. The H100 runs from $3.99 to $12.29, about three times. The B200 runs from $6.69 to $14.21, about twice. Rate cards also move. In our read on 8 October, Nebius showed $3.85 for an H100. On 3 November it showed $4.50.

...

- CoreWeave says it offers up to 60% off its on-demand prices for committed use. That is its own claim. The page lists no committed rate.
- Azure publishes reservation prices through its public price API. For the H100 machine in East US, the one-year price works out 36% below pay as you go and the three-year price 56% below. We divided each term price by its hours.

...

For the H200 they are $9.64 for one year and $8.57 for three, which is 10% and 20% below $10.71.
- E2E Networks says three-month, six-month and annual commitments can earn 10% to 30%, depending on length and volume.
- Sakura Internet announced on 1 July 2026 a commitment plan for one H100 plan: 5% off for six months and 10% off for twelve.
- AWS cut P5 (H100) prices by 44% for on-demand and 45% for the three-year Instance Savings Plan from 1 June 2025.

...

Both point large buyers to sales.

results.title: Azure billing and pricing changes
highlights:
Azure pricing changes since 2026-01-01 as a dated log: euro price adjustment, savings plan for databases, end of reservation exchanges, Foundry prices.

...

Azure pricing changes and billing changes since 2026-01-01, as a dated log: one row per change to a price list, a commitment programme, an export format or a billing mechanism, with who it affects and the Microsoft source behind it. A feature without an effect on the bill is not a row. The log starts on 2026-01-01, is extended by the handbook's monthly rescan, and never loses a row: a correction is a new row with its own date. A change that takes effect in the future sits at the top, under the date on which it applies.

...

| Date | What changed | Who is affected | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2027-02-01 | Reservation exchanges end for services a savings plan covers: Virtual Machines (including the switch between standard and premium storage), Dedicated Host, App Service, SQL Database, SQL Managed Instance, Database for PostgreSQL and MySQL, Cosmos DB, DocumentDB. A reservation bought before keeps one final exchange, a renewal after the date counts as a new purchase; the cancellation policy, instance size flexibility and the trade-in for a savings plan stay. Announced on 2026-07-30 | Everyone holding compute or database reservations | Changes to the Azure reservation exchange policy |
| 2026-10-12 | Flex processing (preview): Azure OpenAI requests with service_tier flex on Global Standard deployments cost half the Standard token rate, without a latency SLA, on their own Flex meters; the first model is gpt-5.6-sol; a request rejected for lack of capacity is not billed | Delay-tolerant Azure OpenAI workloads | Flex processing |
| 2026-09-01 | Microsoft Foundry deployments outside the global pool cost more: EU Data Zone 20 percent above Global (10 before), regional deployments outside the US 25 to 50 percent above Global (Germany 30, France and the UK 40, EU North and EU West 50); pay as you go only for models released from this date on, provisioned throughput for all. Announced on 2026-07-09 | Azure OpenAI and Foundry models in the EU Data Zone or European regions | Foundry model deployment pricing update |
| 2026-06-17 | GitHub Pre-Purchase Plans: twelve-month prepaid commitments bought as Azure reservations, up to 15 percent off GitHub usage (Copilot, Enterprise, Advanced Security, Actions, AI Credits) billed through the linked Azure subscription; unused units expire at the end of the term | Organizations paying for GitHub through Azure | GitHub Pre-Purchase Plans |
| 2026-03-18 | Savings plan for databases: an hourly spend commitment across Azure SQL Database, SQL Managed Instance, Database for PostgreSQL and MySQL, Cosmos DB, DocumentDB and the Database Migration Service, one or three years, up to 35 percent against pay-as-you-go prices | Database workloads without a reservation | Announcing savings plan for databases |
| 2026-02-01 | Commercial Cloud list prices in local currencies move towards the USD level: EUR minus 7.4 percent, CHF minus 9.5, DKK minus 7.4, NOK minus 7.2, SEK minus 13.5; on-premises licences unchanged. Announced on 2025-12-12 | Every customer billed in those currencies | Local currency price adjustments |

...

A list price change in local currency (the euro adjustment of 2026-02-01) lowers the rate per meter from the effective date: in the `UnitPrice` and `EffectivePrice` columns of the actual cost export, in `ListUnitPrice` and `ContractedUnitPrice` of the FOCUS export. Comparing with the January price sheet shows the difference per meter, and per SKU it differs slightly from the announced 7.4 percent through rounding. Customers on a Microsoft Customer Agreement also see the monthly rate at which USD prices are converted into euro; customers on an Enterprise Agreement see the euro list price itself. A euro budget built on the old prices runs under plan from February without any change in usage. The columns are described in Azure cost exports, the currency question in EUR and GBP reporting.

results.title: GPU Cloud Pricing Index, November 2026: H100 to B300
highlights:
## What moved in 2026

- Prices are rising again for flagships. At least one large specialist cloud announced increases of 10 to 26% on H100, H200 and B300 from December 1.
- Clusters cost more than single instances. Multi-node offers are commonly 20 to 50% more per GPU than on-demand single servers.
- Listed is not available. Several providers list GPUs with no deployable region, or “contact sales” for every flagship.
- Fees moved to storage and idle time. Egress is mostly free; stopped-instance storage, public IPs and minimum billing periods are where extra cost appears.

highlights:
AWS is raising GPU instance prices by ~20% on July 1 — and quietly keeping its own Trainium chips at the same price.

This is the most important AI infrastructure pricing story of the year, and the signal is unmistakable.

The move: ~20% price increase on EC2 Capacity Block reservations for Nvidia GPU instances, effective July 1. AWS cited "supply and demand dynamics" — meaning the global compute crunch has gotten severe enough that AWS believes customers will pay more without leaving.
